title: Fixed baseline shares make heterogeneous positive rate-state responses log-convex in cumulative earthquake count
abstract: We extend a published homogeneous rate-state response test to heterogeneous populations with fixed shares of a changing counterfactual baseline. Friction scales, source densities, local loading histories and positive stress-step sizes can differ. The total excess divided by baseline rate is a positive exponential mixture in cumulative baseline count. It is completely monotone and log-convex; its effective count decay rate cannot increase. We prove this necessary condition, give a midpoint inequality, and check 100 synthetic mixtures. A decreasing synthetic excess with increasing count decay fails the condition. Stationary tapered Omori kernels can pass, so passing does not identify the mechanism. We independently reproduce the prior homogeneous result with 75 ODE checks and an Oklahoma aggregate endpoint example. That reproduction is supporting evidence, not the new contribution. No catalog is refitted. The method requires fixed baseline shares, positive stress steps, constant normal stress within each population, and a valid paired baseline. It supplies a conditional test under heterogeneity, not an estimate of the residual Oklahoma driver.

display.caption: Fixed-share positive rate-state mixtures have a decreasing effective decay rate in cumulative baseline count. A synthetic decreasing excess can fail that requirement.
Independent replication of the prior changing-baseline mechanism. This is a model example, not an Oklahoma catalog fit.

citations.reason: We independently reproduce the homogeneous identity and extend its shape test to fixed-share heterogeneous populations.
